subject: Nimbus POC: perf constraints, IO window impact & canary plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@nimhealth.com>, Eric Zhao <eric.zhao@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus POC — post-call recap and immediate asks

Thanks for the time today — good alignment on goals. Short recap and concrete asks to keep momentum.

TL;DR
- Nimbus wants a POC demonstrating sub-200ms p50 for short replies and sub-700ms p95 for larger turns at expected concurrency.
- Streaming needed for transcription-first UX (partial tokens as they arrive).
- Typical sample sizes: ~900 input tokens average, 3–4 outputs averaging 120 tokens; worst-case input spikes to ~8k tokens for multi-doc context.

What we captured (notes):
- SLO targets: p50 <= 200ms (short form answers), p95 <= 700ms (longer responses).
- Expected sustained concurrency during clinic hours: 40–60 concurrent end-users; peak spikes up to ~160 concurrent sessions.
- Throughput: target 10k requests/hour initially, ramp to 50k over 4 weeks.
- Streaming: client requires token-by-token stream with resume-on-reconnect semantics; partial outputs should be visible within 150–250ms of first token generation.
- Context window: primary flows use ~1–2k input tokens; investigative flows may require up to 12k input tokens (history + attachments).

Open asks (action items):
1) Nora/Eric: share a 2–3 day sample (anonymized) of three representative request types (short Q, diagnostic-long, multi-doc ingestion) — we can accept JSONL or NDJSON.
2) Confirm retention & PII constraints (we flagged you for Private deployment / VPC option) — any stricter requirements?
3) Sign off on baseline POC canary: 2-week Dedicated capacity with 10% canary traffic, then 50% before GA.

What we'll do on our side:
- Baseline perf plan: we’ll provision a Dedicated pool with two model variants (medium and heavy) and a routing policy that falls back to the medium variant under load.
- Quantization options: test int8 and quant-4 to estimate token-latency tradeoffs.
- Monitoring: per-token latency traces, queueing depth, and prefix cache hit rates surfaced in Redwood Console.

Attachments: Nimbus-POC-MAP-v0.2.pdf (mutual action plan), sample-payloads.jsonl (example payloads).

Next step: Nora/Eric to send sample payloads + confirm the two-week canary window by EOD Wednesday. If you prefer, I can schedule a short technical sync with our infra lead (Marissa) to run through the stream/connectivity specifics.

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Nimbus POC — post-call recap and immediate asks

Thanks, Connor — helpful recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: we can provide the sample payloads by EOD tomorrow. A few notes up front: 

- Average/expected token sizes: short Q samples average ~180 input tokens; diagnostic-long ~2k tokens; multi-doc ingestion varies but our ETL packs ~6–9k tokens per request for patient history + attachments (we can trim attachments to references if the POC env requires it).
- Streaming requirement is mandatory: our UX shows partial sentences as clinicians type; we need the first partial output within ~200ms and the experience should be smooth when the model emits long outputs (chunked).
- Latency tolerance: front-line clinicians consider anything >800ms for a long response as disruptive; your p95 700ms target is aligned.

Question: are you proposing the Dedicated pool to be in our VPC? We need the Dedicated capacity in our US-East region and integration with our KMS for key handling. Also, what are the fallback semantics if heavy model runs out of capacity?

I attached our internal requirements sheet (nim_health_requirements.xlsx) — it includes retention, encryption, and audit cadence.

On canary length: 2 weeks sounds fine but we need a rollback plan and traffic shaping so only 10% of sessions in prod hit the POC cluster initially.

Thanks — Nora

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Nimbus POC — post-call recap and immediate asks

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Nora — and thanks for the sheet. I wanted to add concrete perf tradeoffs so you can make an informed sign-off.

Context-window and latency: practical guidance
- Baseline suggestion for the POC: provision Dedicated pool sized for 80 concurrent model sessions on the heavy variant (handles large 8–12k IO windows) and 200 concurrent on the medium variant (optimized for 1–3k windows).
- Measured behavior (typical Redwood profiles):
  * Heavy variant (12k I/O combined): p50 token-latency 60–85ms, p95 token-latency 340–520ms depending on quantization and batching. End-to-end response p95 for large outputs ~650–900ms (depends on output token count and streaming chunking).
  * Medium variant (<=3k I/O): p50 token-latency 18–35ms, p95 120–210ms; end-to-end p95 often <350ms for 100–300 token outputs.

Key tradeoffs and mitigations
- KV cache and prefix caching: for repeated patient-context lookups we recommend enabling prefix caching (saves 30–60% of token compute for similar contexts).
- Batching vs latency: batching increases throughput but adds queueing delay — configure auto-batching with a 20ms max queue timeout for interactive UX.
- Quantization: int8 gives cost savings but may increase p95 by ~10–15% on heavy-window flows; we’ll profile quant-4 for a better cost/latency sweet spot.
- Streaming chunk size: emitting ~32–64 tokens per chunk tends to balance perceived responsiveness and network overhead.

Canary/fallback semantics
- Initial routing: 10% of traffic -> Dedicated POC cluster, 90% -> existing hosted endpoint. All requests carry request-id metadata so we can trace misses.
- Fallback: when heavy variant queue > threshold or latency alarm fires (p95 latency > 2x target), traffic gracefully routes to medium variant with a best-effort de-prioritization of non-critical tokens (truncate long histories) — client will receive a header indicating a degraded-mode.
- Rollback: instant traffic cutover to hosted endpoints + notification to your SREs; we’ll also drain queues to minimize partial-output duplication.

Immediate asks for sign-off:
1) Approve Dedicated pool in US-East and our proposed concurrency sizing above.
2) Confirm KMS integration window (we need key handshake and billing account connection 5 business days before kickoff).
3) Share a trimmed 24-hour sample of the heavy multi-doc flow (we’ll use the example to size the prefix cache).

Attachments: canary-runbook.md (runbook + rollback steps).

If that looks good I suggest we lock the capacity numbers and I’ll schedule a technical kickoff for next Tue (30 min).

—
Marissa Cole
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Dedicated
